title: Photonic Time Crystals — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Photonic Time Crystals' rich face, its first round, a Sketch and still a proposal: the key reversal walked up to a test (a stack of layers and a Yee grid, sharing no code, giving one exponent, with the gap on the frequency axis in space and the wave-number axis in time), the first open question put to its strongest rivals (a time mirror is a reverse plus varispeed or a comb, in the ideal), and two pieces gathered from the Floquet and parametric faces beside the sentences they test. I grow when the page is enriched again; I never hold the entry's words.

pieces.file: /Floquet Theory/Floquet Theory — rich — same equation twice.html
pieces.title: same equation, read twice · from Floquet Theory's face
pieces.caption: **Bloch in space, Floquet in time, checked.** Made for [[Floquet Theory]] and gathered here because it tests this sentence for the simplest case: a wave in a cosine lattice and a spring pumped in time are one equation, and the lattice's gap edges, found from plane waves, are the spring's tongue edges, found by integration, within 2 × 10⁻⁷, with half the trace of one period's map equal to cos kπ inside every band. It also pins the dictionary: Bloch's k is the imaginary part of the Floquet exponent, not the exponent. Still a proposal on its own page.

pieces.file: Photonic Time Crystals — rich — a gap in momentum.html
pieces.by: thin-layer stack · Yee grid · Web Audio Worklet
pieces.title: a gap in momentum
pieces.caption: **The key reversal, walked up and measured.** One wave in a plain medium; a stack of sinusoidal layers, where a band of frequencies dies with depth (×e^(−0.157) a cell at the centre, m = 0.1); a ring whose 1/ε breathes, where a forward wave in the gap grows and calls up a backward partner that reaches its size (B/F 0.9998 after 30 periods); the gap heard, a whisper of noise swelling to one pitch, half the pump, even with the pump between two of the ring's modes (441.25 Hz, between 440 and 442.5). That could fail: two free modes at 440 and 442.5 read about 442.25 Hz on the same count, with two lines and a 14 dB beat. Then the test, its pass rule stated first. A stack of 2000 thin layers a cell and a Yee grid of 8192 cells share no code and give the same exponent: 0.15690 against 0.15689 at the centre, worst 2.9 × 10⁻³ at an edge, where the rate climbs steeply. And the axis turns: in space the gap is a band of frequencies, all at the zone edge; in time it is a band of wave numbers, every one at exactly half the breathing rate. The page says frequencies; measured, it is a momentum gap.
pieces.near: The same exponential structure, but pointing in dual directions

pieces.file: /Parametric Resonance/Parametric Resonance — rich — the threshold heard.html
pieces.title: the threshold, heard · from Parametric Resonance's face
pieces.caption: **The crack the hook names.** Made for [[Parametric Resonance]] and gathered beside this sentence so the threshold can be felt before the connection is read: one 220 Hz ring pumped at 440 Hz, decaying below threshold, then a noise floor 80 dB down swelling into a steady tone once the pump passes 4ζ. That 4ζ is in its page's ε; in the gap piece above, which writes the breathing as 1 + 2m cos, the same threshold reads m = 2ζ. It is the single-mode case of the gap piece above: one wave number, sitting in the gap. Still a proposal on its own page.
pieces.near: of parametric threshold and reads this connection

verdicts.file: Photonic Time Crystals — rich — a mirror in time.html
verdicts.why: Its test is against a plain reverse buffer only; a reverse buffer varispeeded by n₁/n₂ at gain r_E matches the single jump to −86 dB, and one through a two-tap comb matches the there-and-back to −318 dB. Add those two nulls to step 4, state the verdict rule before the trial and make the bold headlines depend on it, re-word the answer (distinct from a plain reverse, reproducible by varispeed or comb in the ideal line), and update the Open Questions offer to match.

pieces.file: Photonic Time Crystals — rich — a mirror in time.html
pieces.by: uniform line, forward and backward parts · Yee grid
pieces.title: a mirror in time
pieces.caption: **The first question, put to the strongest rivals.** A phrase of four notes sent back by a wall (same order); by a jump of the whole line's index (reversed, transposed by n₁/n₂ and stretched by n₂/n₁: at n₂ = 2 the held A4 returns at 220.00 Hz, 2.80 s long, −18.1 dB); by a jump and a jump back 1 ms later (reversed at pitch but combed). Then two digital rivals built from the rule's numbers, and a rule stated before the trial: a mirror is a sound of its own only if no chain of reverse, varispeed and comb comes within −40 dB of it. A plain reverse misses both by about 0 dB, but a reverse slowed and scaled matches the single jump to −105 dB, and a reverse through a two-tap comb matches the there-and-back to −318 dB. So in this ideal line a time mirror is a reverse plus one operation, varispeed or comb. What could give a real one its own sound lies outside the ideal: finite rise, dispersion, gain in a crystal. The mixing rule is checked against a Yee grid that knows nothing of it, within 0.5 %.
pieces.near: A time-modulated audio system can, in principle, time-reverse incident audio

offers.what: “Ranges of frequencies that propagate without amplification (allowed bands) interspersed with ranges that grow exponentially in time (bandgaps)”: in a medium uniform in space every wave keeps its wave number, so the gap is a range of wave numbers, a momentum gap, and every mode inside it oscillates at exactly half the modulation rate. Measured at m = 0.1 on a Yee grid of 8192 cells: the 7 wave numbers from ν = 0.9531 to 1.0469 grow, each turned by π a period to 3 × 10⁻¹⁶; the spatial stack's gap at the same m is the frequency range ν = 0.9530 to 1.0533, each at a Bloch phase of π a cell; the exponents match (0.15690 against 0.15689 at the centre). So the reversal is double: decay in space becomes growth in time, and the gap moves from the frequency axis to the wave-number axis. Suggest: “ranges of wave numbers that propagate (allowed bands) interspersed with ranges — momentum gaps — where every mode oscillates at half the modulation frequency and grows exponentially in time”, the two bullets naming the axis, and the intro's “frequency bandgaps” as “momentum bandgaps”.

“Time-reflection … incident light at bandgap frequencies has its phase conjugated, time-reversed, and re-emitted.” A single sudden change of the whole medium's index reflects every frequency, not only the gap's: D and B stay continuous, the wave number stays, the frequency scales by n₁/n₂, and the backward electric field is n₁(n₁ − n₂)/(2n₂²) of the incoming. A Yee grid that knows nothing of that rule gives, at n₂ = 2, backward D 0.4994 against 0.5 and frequency 0.4995 against 0.5. That broadband reflection is what Moussa et al. observed in 2023. A time crystal's periodic modulation is what makes the reflection resonant, and amplifying, at the momentum gap. Suggest: “a sudden change of the medium's index sends part of every wave back, phase-conjugated and shifted in frequency by n₁/n₂; a time crystal's periodic modulation makes this resonant and amplifying in its momentum gap.”

The first question now has a measured partial answer, in an ideal line (lossless, no dispersion, instant jumps). One jump of the index: the phrase returns reversed, transposed by n₁/n₂ and stretched by n₂/n₁ (A4 → 220.00 Hz and 2.80 s at n₂ = 2), at 20 log|n₁(n₁ − n₂)/(2n₂²)|, −18.06 dB at n₂ = 2. A jump and a jump back τ later: reversed at its own pitch but combed, |r(f)| = ½|n₂/n₁ − n₁/n₂| |sin(2πfτ n₁/n₂)|. Neither is a plain reverse buffer (residual about 0 dB), but each is a reverse buffer plus one known operation: read n₂/n₁ times slower and scaled by r_E (residual −96 to −105 dB), or through a two-tap comb ±¼(n₂/n₁ − n₁/n₂), 2τn₁/n₂ apart (−318 dB at τ = 1 ms; −90 dB at a fractional τ). So the honest answer is which operation, not 'distinct by ear': in the ideal a time mirror is varispeed-reverse or comb-reverse, and a sound of its own would have to come from what the ideal leaves out (finite rise time, dispersion, gain in a crystal's momentum gap). Suggest a clause on the bullet saying so and pointing at the piece; 'nobody has built the audio version' still stands.

Two lines. “Modulation in the hundreds of THz range” for ~500 THz light: the momentum gap opens where the wave's frequency is half the modulation rate, so it needs about 1000 THz (1 PHz). And “modulating at GHz to THz … produces small-signal time-crystal physics”: a slow modulation puts the light in a high tongue of the same equation, and for a sinusoidal modulation the higher tongues fade fast. Peak growth per pump period at m = 0.05: 0.0786, 0.00786, 0.000747, 0.0000700 for tongues 1 to 4 (the challenger's mpmath values; mine agreed to about 15 %); at m = 0.01, 0.0157, 0.000314, 0.0000060, about fiftyfold a tongue. A square wave does not fade this way (its odd tongues stay first order), so the clean reason is spectral: a sinusoid slower than the light has no Fourier content at twice the light's frequency. What slow or single-cycle modulation gives instead is time refraction, a frequency shift, which is what the ITO experiments measured (from the literature, not the piece). Suggest naming the 2:1 condition and calling the slow regime time refraction.

From the literature, not from a piece; sources are web, not canon. (1) 2022 time-reflection: Moussa, Xu, Yin, Galiffi, Ra'di and Alù (CUNY), arXiv 2208.07236 (Aug 2022), Nature Physics 19, 863–868 (2023), in a transmission-line metamaterial switched uniformly in time, with signals at 30–70 MHz (RF, not microwave) and a switch rise of about 3 ns; it also paired two interfaces into a temporal Fabry–Pérot. No source was found for a 'Caloz group' observation: drop the name. (2) 2009: no source was found for 'J. Lukens et al.': drop it. The 2009 paper is Zurita-Sánchez, Halevi and Cervantes-González, Phys. Rev. A 79, 053821 (2009), with forbidden wave-vector gaps. (3) '2018–2020: first experimental demonstrations' is too late: a k gap was measured in 2015 in a dynamic microwave transmission line (Reyes-Ayona and Halevi, Appl. Phys. Lett. 107, 2015, doi 10.1063/1.4928659), and time reflection of water waves was observed in 2016 (Bacot, Labousse, Eddi, Fink and Fort, Nature Physics). (4) Momentum-gap amplification in a microwave metasurface: Wang, Mirmoosa, Asadchy, Rockstuhl, Fan and Tretyakov, Science Advances 9, eadg7541 (2023).
